title: Clock and Compass
premise: In the winter of 1813, during a brutal continental campaign, battlefield nurse Mara Montrose secretly records the names of soldiers that officers strike from official rolls—men written off as deserters or dead to hide casualties and desertion. When a gaunt stranger named Elias Vane arrives at her dressing station carrying letters in the handwriting of Captain Aldous Reeve, a man officially dead and whose 'death' Mara's ledger quietly contradicts, she realizes the army is erasing a mutiny and its witnesses. Hunted by the officer who authored the cover-up, Mara and Elias must carry Reeve's letters and her ledger past three checkpoints to a war correspondent before the river ice breaks and seals the evidence—and them—behind enemy lines. They reach the correspondent at terrible cost, Elias dying at the third checkpoint, and the published truth saves the surviving accused men even as Mara finally writes her own name into the ledger she kept for everyone else.
about_author: Kestrel Joubert is the pen name of a former military archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records and the gaps between them. Fascinated by the clerks, nurses, and quartermasters who kept history's real books, Joubert writes fiction from the margins of official accounts.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Linen
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At a freezing dressing station, Mara treats the wounded by day and records omitted names by night, hiding the ledger in a linen trunk. When an officer demands she burn a dead private's effects, she quietly copies his name instead. Emotional beat: quiet, disciplined defiance established.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Sentry Line
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Elias Vane collapses at the perimeter, half-frozen, carrying a satchel he refuses to surrender. He claims to be a paymaster's clerk, but Mara notices army-issue boots and a soldier's calluses. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; Mara's instinct to protect the overlooked extends to him.

chapters.title: Handwriting of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sorting Elias's belongings for lice, Mara finds letters signed by Captain Aldous Reeve—dated after Reeve's official death, which she personally recorded. She confronts Elias, who admits Reeve is alive, hidden with eleven accused mutineers awaiting summary execution. Emotional beat: the ledger's quiet truth becomes a live, dangerous thing.

chapters.title: What the Colonel Struck Out
chapters.summary: Elias's POV flashback. Elias recounts the winter march, the starvation rations, the mutiny at Vosk Bridge, and Colonel Hargreave's decision to record the twelve men as deserters already executed—except Reeve escaped. Emotional beat: righteous anger tempered by guilt; Elias was the clerk who typed the lie.

chapters.title: The Correspondent at Thorn Mill
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Elias reveals his plan: deliver the letters and Mara's ledger to war correspondent Samuel Okafor at Thorn Mill, beyond three checkpoints, before the river ice breaks and cuts the route. Mara hesitates—exposure means the gallows for her too. Emotional beat: the choice between invisibility and consequence.

chapters.title: Twelve Names, One Omission
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reviews her ledger and realizes she recorded eleven mutineers but never learned Reeve's fate—her one omission. She agrees to go, but only if Elias helps her complete the record. Emotional beat: her compulsion for truth becomes personal; the found-family bond begins.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Colonel Hargreave summons Mara to treat his gout, probing about the stranger in her ward. She plays the invisible nurse perfectly, but he mentions a missing satchel. Emotional beat: cold dread; the hunter has begun circling, and Mara's performance of harmlessness is her armor.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Disguised as a burial detail, Mara and Elias pass the first checkpoint by reading aloud the names of the dead to a superstitious sergeant—including, at Elias's insistence, the twelve 'deserters.' Emotional beat: the names as incantation and shield; first taste of open defiance.

chapters.title: The Ice Road
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Crossing the frozen river at night, Elias confesses he forged part of Hargreave's order and fears his own testimony damns him as much as the colonel. Mara refuses absolution but offers partnership. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by truth; they choose each other over clean hands.

chapters.title: The Informant at the Chapel
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A chaplain who once treated Mara's wounded offers shelter, then betrays them to Hargreave's dragoons for a promotion. They escape through the crypt as soldiers search above. Emotional beat: betrayal wounds; trust must now be rationed like food.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Surgeon's Table
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the second checkpoint, the examining surgeon recognizes Mara from a field hospital and hesitates. Mara gambles, telling him the truth about the twelve men. He stamps their papers through, then burns his own copy of the casualty roll. Emotional beat: the ledger's cause spreads; complicity becomes solidarity.

chapters.title: What Reeve Wrote
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Reading Reeve's letters aloud by candlelight, they learn Hargreave sold the regiment's rations and blamed the resulting mutiny on the men who protested. Elias breaks down—he had suspected and stayed silent. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve; the mission is now a reckoning.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Net
chapters.summary: Hargreave's POV. Hargreave closes the roads, posts a reward for a nurse and a clerk, and orders the twelve prisoners' execution moved up to the day the ice breaks. Emotional beat: antagonist given full weight—vain, frightened, genuinely believing order matters more than truth.

chapters.title: The Orphan of the baggage Train
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A fourteen-year-old baggage-train orphan, Tamsin, catches them hiding and blackmails her way into the party. Mara, who has buried too many children, can't turn her away. Emotional beat: found family crystallizes; Mara now has something to lose beyond herself.

chapters.title: The Frozen Ford
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Detouring to avoid a roadblock, they cross a ford where the ice groans; Tamsin falls through and Elias pulls her out, wrecking the satchel's oilskin. Mara sacrifices her cloak to rewrap the letters. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness; the river becomes the story's ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Gallows Field
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The third checkpoint sits beside the execution ground where the twelve are to die. Hargreave himself inspects papers. Mara, recognized, stalls him with a fabricated epidemic report while Elias slips the ledger and letters through the wire to a waiting runner. Emotional beat: maximum tension; her invisibility finally spent as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hargreave orders both arrested. As the river ice cracks like cannon fire, Elias draws the dragoons away across the thawing ford and goes under with the satchel's empty oilskin, buying Mara her escape. Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice; loyalty fulfilled at the ultimate price of survival.

chapters.title: The Empty Satchel
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Grieving, Mara learns the runner reached Okafor with the letters—but her ledger, her twelve names and years of quiet record, went into the river with Elias. Emotional beat: hollowed-out sorrow; the question of whether truth needs its witness.

chapters.title: The Trial of Colonel Hargreave
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Okafor's dispatches ignite scandal; Hargreave is court-martialed and summons Mara as a witness. She testifies from memory, reciting every name she ever recorded, including the eleven men reprieved at the last hour. Emotional beat: the ledger lives in her; truth spoken aloud becomes testimony.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Offered a regimental apprenticeship as reward for silence, Tamsin instead publicly corroborates Mara's account, choosing the makeshift family over safety. Emotional beat: the found family's values passed to the next generation; courage inherited.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At Thorn Mill, Okafor publishes the full account, and the eleven surviving accused men—Reeve among them—march past Mara in the spring mud. Reeve stops, reads the reconstructed list she has rewritten from memory, and salutes her. Emotional beat: vindication and grief braided; the dead and saved share one page.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a new ledger bought with her discharge pay, Mara writes the first entry: Elias Vane, clerk, who chose the truth—and beneath it, for the first time, her own name, Mara Montrose, nurse. She and Tamsin walk toward a civilian hospital that will have them. Emotional beat: resolution; the woman who recorded everyone finally counts herself.
